title: Determination of Zeta Potential via Nanoparticle Translocation Velocities through a Tunable Nanopore: Using DNA-modified Particles as an Example
protocol: Dissolve one PBS tablet in 200 ml deionized water.
Add 100 μl of Tween-20 to the buffer solution.
Vortex calibration particles for 30 seconds before sonication for 2 minutes at 80 watts.
Dilute calibration particles 1 in 100 to a concentration of 1x10^10 particles/ml in PBST buffer.
Vortex diluted calibration particles for 30 seconds.
Vortex streptavidin coated particles for 30 seconds before sonication for 2 minutes at 80 watts.
Dilute streptavidin coated particles 1 in 100 in PBST buffer to achieve a concentration of 1x10^9 particles/ml.
Vortex diluted streptavidin coated particles for 30 seconds.
Reconstitute oligonucleotides with deionized water to a concentration of 100 µM.
Vortex the streptavidin coated particles (200 μl sample volume) for 30 seconds before sonication for 2 minutes at 80 watts.
Add the appropriate concentration of DNA to the particles for resulting concentrations of 10, 20, 30, 40, 47, 95, 140, and 210 nM DNA.
Vortex the samples for 10 sec.
Place the samples on a rotary wheel at room temperature for 30 min to allow DNA to bind to particle surfaces via streptavidin-biotin interaction.
Remove excess DNA in solution via magnetic separation by placing samples onto a magnetic rack for 30 min.
Carefully remove supernatant without disturbing particles closest to magnet.
Replace supernatant with the same volume of new PBST buffer.
Add target DNA at 500 nM to ensure maximum binding was reached.
Vortex the samples for 10 sec.
Place samples on a rotary wheel at room temperature for 30 min.
Remove excess target DNA via magnetic separation by placing samples onto a magnetic rack for 30 min.
Carefully remove supernatant without disturbing particles closest to magnet.
Replace supernatant with same volume of new PBST buffer.
Repeat steps involving hybridization and washing for duplicate samples.
Place these samples on a rotary wheel at room temperature for 16 hours to investigate DNA hybridization times.
Plug in the TRPS instrument to a computer system with installed software.
Calibrate the initial stretch using a caliper.
Measure the distance between the outside of two parallel jaws.
Input the measured distance into the 'stretch' field in the 'Instrument Settings' tab.
Click 'Calibrate stretch' underneath the tab.
Fit a polyurethane nanopore membrane onto the jaws with the ID number facing upward.
Stretch the jaws to 43-48 mm using the stretch adjustment handle.
Place 80 µl of PBST buffer in the lower fluid cell, ensuring no bubbles are present.
Replace the buffer if any bubbles are observed.
Click the upper fluid cell into place.
Add 40 µl of buffer to the upper fluid cell.
Ensure there are no bubbles in the upper fluid cell.
Remove and replace the liquid if bubbles are present.
Vortex samples for 30 seconds.
Sonicate samples for 2 minutes at 80 watts prior to TRPS analysis.
Place 40 µl of calibration particles (1x10^10 particles/ml) into the upper fluid cell.
Complete a TRPS measurement at 3 applied voltages.
Increase or decrease voltage by clicking on the '+' and '-' buttons in the 'Instrument Settings' tab.
Verify that background currents are approximately 140, 110, and 80 nA for each of the three voltages.
Ensure calibration particles produce an average blockade magnitude of at least 0.3 nA at medium voltage.
Apply pressure so the average full width half maximum (FWHM) durations of calibration particles are at least 0.15 msec.
Select pressure or vacuum by rotating the arm until it clicks into the desired position and apply accordingly.
Start the run by clicking 'start' on the software in the 'Data Acquisition' tab.
Complete the run by pressing 'stop' when at least 500 particles have been measured and the run has exceeded 30 seconds.
Calibrate the system every time a new nanopore is introduced or for each new day of analysis.
Run samples at the highest or second highest voltage to achieve a similar baseline current.
Replace the electrolyte in the upper fluid cell with 40 µl of sample.
Start the sample run by clicking 'start' in the 'Data Acquisition' tab.
Record a minimum of 500 particles during the run time, ensuring it is at least 30 seconds.
Click 'stop' in the 'Data Acquisition' tab to complete the measurement.
Save the data file.
Wash the system by placing 40 μl of PBST buffer into the upper fluid cell several times.
Apply various pressures (usually at -10, -5 cm (vacuum), and 5 and 10 cm (positive pressure)) until no more blockade events are present.
Ensure there are no residual particles remaining in the system to prevent cross contamination between samples.
